oracle.precisionAgreement: expected binary64 bits/error plus interval endpoints are identical at both precisions
oracle.input: Exact signed binary64 dyadic converted using BigInt to a terminating decimal string; no Number.toString conversion.
oracle.degrees: Signed exact BigInt modulo360 centered to [-180,180], then high-precision multiplication by pi/180. Inverse functions return degrees.
oracle.trigonometry: Independent sine/cosine entire Taylor series using Decimal arithmetic on |radians|<=pi; stop when the sum is unchanged at the requested precision, at most2048 terms. tan=sin/cos. Avoids decimal.js public trig's precision+argument.sd pi-limit amplification without shrinking inputs/precision.
oracle.rounding: Exact integer/rational binary64 round-to-nearest ties-to-even of the high-precision Decimal result; public zero normalized to +0.
oracle.fourUlp: Correctly rounded binary64 reference r, abs(y-r)<=4*ulp(r), evaluated as exact rationals. ulp(r)=2^(floor(log2(abs(r)))-52), or 2^-1074 for zero/subnormal. lower/upper are ceil/floor of that absolute interval intersected with finite binary64 outputs, not four adjacent steps.
oracle.exact: Entries marked exact require their stated representative value/pole exactly; no ULP tolerance supersedes domain or exact representatives.
limitations: Finite corpus and two-precision convergence are not proof over every finite input.
Two precisions share decimal.js algorithms and constants; matching results cannot exclude shared-library defects.

Decimal transcendental outputs are high-precision approximations, not formally directed real enclosures. Their converged binary64 rounding is an independent test reference, not a universal correct-rounding certificate.
Fixed pi and ln10 constants have 1025 digits; requested400/800 significant digits plus internal guards remain below that limit.
Existing abs/floor/ceiling/sqrt have separate evidence and are not included here.
